seoTitle: How to Assign Tasks in Google Workspace via Google Chat
metaDescription: Learn how to assign tasks to teammates directly inside Google Chat using Google Workspace's built-in Tasks integration and smart chips.
intro: Switching between chat and a separate task manager slows teams down. Google Workspace lets you assign tasks directly inside Google Chat conversations, keeping communication and accountability in one place. This guide shows how to set it up.

steps.heading: Open a Google Chat conversation
steps.body: Start from any direct message or space where you want to assign a task to a team member.

steps.heading: Create a task using the built-in integration
steps.body: Use Google Chat's Tasks integration or smart chips to create a new task directly within the conversation.

steps.heading: Assign the task to a specific person
steps.body: Select the teammate responsible for the task so it appears in their personal task list and the shared conversation.

steps.heading: Set a due date
steps.body: Add a deadline to the task so everyone involved knows when it needs to be completed.

steps.heading: Track progress within Chat
steps.body: Check task status directly inside the conversation, keeping the whole team updated without needing a separate project management tool.

faq.question: Do I need a specific Google Workspace plan to assign tasks in Chat?
faq.answer: This feature works across Business Starter, Standard, and Education accounts, though exact availability can vary by plan.

faq.question: Can I assign tasks in Google Chat from the Gmail interface too?
faq.answer: Yes, since Google Chat is integrated into Gmail, you can access and assign tasks from either the Gmail sidebar or the standalone Chat app.

faq.question: Will the assigned person get a notification?
faq.answer: Yes, assigning a task typically triggers a notification so the person knows a new task has been added to their list.

faq.question: Can I set recurring tasks through Google Chat?
faq.answer: The basic assignment flow covers one-time tasks with due dates; more advanced recurring task setups may require Google Tasks directly.
